summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a NAT gateway on its eth1 interface (10.50.50.254/24, the private network shared with node2/node3), with a source-NAT masquerade rule translating 10.50.50.0/24 traffic out eth0 to the internet. node2 (10.50.50.11) and node3 (10.50.50.12) were given static eth1 addresses and a secondary default route via node1 (metric 200, below the pre-existing eth0 control-plane default), plus rp_filter=0 on eth1 to stop strict reverse-path filtering from dropping asymmetric replies (the only real bug found, confirmed via tcpdump). End-to-end verified via eth1-bound ping and HTTPS from both node2 and node3, with tcpdump on node1 showing correct request/reply masquerade translation between eth1 and eth0. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured baseline boot_id and health, rebooted each node individually, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified NAT config, routes, rp_filter setting, and live internet connectivity through node1 after each restart. All three nodes recovered fully with persisted configuration.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network topology (eth0 control-plane network, eth1 unconfigured private network)
Configured VyOS node1: eth1 address 10.50.50.254/24, NAT source masquerade rule 100 for 10.50.50.0/24 out eth0, committed and saved
Configured node2 eth1 static IP 10.50.50.11/24 via nmcli with default route via 10.50.50.254 metric 200
Configured node3 eth1 static IP 10.50.50.12/24 via nmcli with default route via 10.50.50.254 metric 200
Diagnosed and fixed rp_filter=1 on eth1 (node2, node3) causing asymmetric reverse-path drops of NAT replies; persisted via /etc/sysctl.d/98-eth1-rpfilter.conf
Verified NAT end-to-end with ping and curl over eth1 from node2 and node3, and tcpdump on node1 eth1/eth0 showing masquerade translation
Captured baseline boot_id and health on all 3 nodes
Rebooted node1, polled until exec recovered, confirmed boot_id change, reverified NAT rule/interfaces/forwarding and live connectivity from node2/node3
Rebooted node2, polled until exec recovered, confirmed boot_id change, reverified eth1 config/route/rp_filter/connectivity
Rebooted node3, polled until exec recovered, confirmed boot_id change, reverified eth1 config/route/rp_filter/connectivity

evidence.requirement: node1 provides NAT for node2/node3 to reach internet
evidence.summary: NAT masquerade rule configured on node1 (eth1->eth0, 10.50.50.0/24); tcpdump on node1 shows ICMP request from 10.50.50.11 arriving eth1 and leaving eth0 as 10.100.231.10 with reply un-NATed back; curl HTTPS from node2 and node3 via eth1 succeeds (http_code=301) proving live internet reachability through node1

evidence.requirement: Root cause diagnosis of initial NAT failure (rp_filter asymmetric drop)
evidence.summary: Reply packets arrived on node2/node3 eth1 per tcpdump but ping showed 100% loss; sysctl showed rp_filter=1 on eth1 vs preferred eth0 route to source; disabling rp_filter on eth1 fixed ping immediately on both nodes

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4098161f captured with NAT rule active; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 83b93206 (changed) confirmed via poll; NAT rule/eth1/ip_forward all persisted; node2 and node3 internet access through node1 reverified post-reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline health and restart evidence
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d6298ced captured; reboot triggered (stream closed); post-reboot boot_id 563d7d6d (changed) confirmed; eth1 static IP, default route, rp_filter=0, and live NAT'd HTTPS/ICMP connectivity all recovered
